source_text: VII. Hic autem labor, haec inopia, hoc necessitatis tempus ad deum pertinuit, dilectissimi fratres. nam qui nos temptari voluit, ipse ut adlocutionem in ipsa temptatione haberemus ostendit. nam Victori presbytero commartyri nostro, qui statim post hanc eandem visionem passus est, ostensum est hoc. Videbam, inquit, puerum huc in carcerem introisse, cuius fuit vultus perlucidus super splendorem inenarrabilem. qui nos deducebat per omnia loca ut exiremus; egredi tamen non potuimus, et ait mihi: Adhuc modicum laboratis, quia nunc impedimini. sed confidite quia ego vobiscum sum. et adiecit: Dic illis quia: Gloriosiorem coronam habebitis, nec non: Ad deum suum spiritus properat, et anima iam proxima passioni sedes suas requisivit. nam hunc eundem dominum de paradiso interrogavit ubi esset. cui ille ait: Extra mundum est. Ostende mihi illum, inquit. et ait illi: Et ubi erit fides? eumque hoc per humanam pusillitatem diceret: Quod me mandas tenere non possum, dic signum quod eis dicam, respondit ei dominus et ait: Dic illis signum Iacobi. laetandum est, fratres dilectissimi, ut patriarchis, etsi non iustitia, vel laboribus adaequari possimus. sed qui dixit: Invoca me in die pressurae, et eximam te, et clarificabis me, ad clarificationem sui flexus, post preces ad se habitas commemoratus est nostri, prius miserationis suae denuntians munus. VIII. De hoc enim sorori nostrae Quartillosiae hic nobiscum positae ostendit, cuius mulieris et maritus et filius ante triduum passi erant. ipsa quoque hic residens propinquitatem suam velociter subsecuta est; quae in hunc modum quod vidit exposuit. Vidi, inquit, filium meum, qui passus est, venisse huc ad carcerem; qui sedens super labrum aquarum ait: Vidit deus pressuram vestram et laborem. et post hunc introivit iuvenis mirae magnitudinis portans fialas duas singulis manibus lacte plenas, et ait: Bono animo estote, memoratus est vestri deus. et ex fialis quas ferebat dedit omnibus bibere; quae fialae non deficiebant. et subito ablatus est lapis qui fenestram dividit medius; sed et clarae fenestrae, ipso medio ablato, liberam caeli faciem admiserant. et posuit iuvenis ille quas ferebat fialas, unam ad dexteram, alteram ad sinistram, et ait: Ecce satiati estis et abundat, et tertia adhuc fiala superveniet vobis. et abiit.
pass_a_gloss: Literal gloss: this toil and want and time of necessity pertained to God; he who willed us to be tempted showed that we have an address in temptation itself; this was shown to Victor the presbyter our fellow-martyr who suffered right after the same vision: he saw a boy enter the prison with a very clear face beyond unspeakable splendor leading them through all places to go out but they could not exit, saying they still toil a little because now hindered, but to be confident because he is with them, and adding tell them they will have a more glorious crown, and the spirit hastens to its God and the soul near to passion has sought its seats, and Victor asked the Lord where paradise is, he said outside the world, show it to me, where will faith be, and from human smallness asking for something to hold and a sign to tell them, the Lord said tell them Jacob's sign; it is to be rejoiced that we can be equaled to the patriarchs if not in justice at least in labors; but he who said call on me in the day of pressure and I will take you out and you will make me clear, bent to his own making-clear, after prayers to him remembered us, proclaiming first the gift of his pity; and about this he showed to sister Quartillosia here with us whose husband and son suffered three days before, she herself remaining here quickly followed her kin, and related thus what she saw: she saw her suffered son come to the prison sitting on the lip of the waters saying God saw their pressure and labor, and after him a youth of wondrous size entered carrying two bowls full of milk one in each hand saying be of good mind, God remembered you, and gave all to drink from the bowls and the bowls did not run out, and suddenly the stone dividing the window in the middle was removed and the bright windows with the middle removed let in the free face of heaven, and the youth placed the bowls one to the right one to the left saying behold you are sated and it overflows and still a third bowl will come to you, and he went away.
pass_b_english: But this hardship, this destitution, this season of need had to do with God, dearest brothers.
For he who willed that we be tested himself showed that we should have encouragement in the very testing.
For this was shown to Victor the presbyter, our fellow-martyr, who suffered immediately after this same vision.
I saw, he said, a boy come in here into the prison, whose face was shining clear beyond unspeakable brightness.
He was leading us through every place so that we might go out; yet we could not go forth, and he said to me: You still toil a little while, for now you are held back.
But take courage, for I am with you.
And he added: Tell them: You shall have a more glorious crown, and also: The spirit hastens to its God, and the soul, now close to suffering, has sought out its own seats.
For he questioned this same Lord about paradise, where it was.
To him he said: It is outside the world.
Show it to me, he said.
And he said to him: And where will faith be?
And when he said this through human littleness: What you bid me hold I cannot grasp, tell a sign which I may tell them, the Lord answered him and said: Tell them the sign of Jacob.
It is cause for rejoicing, dearest brothers, that we may be made equal to the patriarchs, if not in righteousness, at least in labors.

But he who said: Call upon me in the day of distress, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me (Psalms 49:15 LXX), bending toward his own glorification, after the prayers made to him remembered us, first announcing the gift of his mercy.
For concerning this he showed to our sister Quartillosia, placed here with us, whose husband and son had suffered three days before.
She also, remaining here, quickly followed her kin; she set forth in this manner what she saw.
I saw, she said, my son, who suffered, come here to the prison; sitting upon the rim of the water-basin he said: God has seen your distress and toil.
And after him there entered a youth of marvelous stature bearing two bowls full of milk, one in each hand, and he said: Be of good courage, God has remembered you.
And from the bowls which he bore he gave to all to drink; and the bowls did not fail.
And suddenly the stone which divided the window in the middle was taken away; but the bright windows, with the middle taken away, admitted the open face of heaven.
And that youth set down the bowls which he bore, one to the right and the other to the left, and said: Behold, you are filled and it abounds, and yet a third bowl shall come to you.
And he departed.

choices.why: in ipsa temptatione context requires consoling address, not formal speech; renders function of divine comfort to prisoners
Iacobi as patriarchal proper name fits preceding patriarchis clause; retains ambiguity rather than resolving to James
plural sedes here denotes resting places sought by soul near suffering, not singular throne
